eLearning & CTRE Support Start here

The eLearning & Center for Teaching and Research Excellence (CTRE) Joint Office is the central hub for faculty development, instructional design, online learning, and academic technology support.

What the office does

The office supports faculty, departments, and academic units in designing high-quality courses, integrating effective teaching strategies, using instructional technologies, and advancing scholarly and professional growth across in-person, hybrid, and online environments. It provides strategic leadership and hands-on support for the learning management system, instructional design, assessment, faculty training, and research development.

Course Assignments & Brightspace Access Read before the term

How you get assigned to a course, how you gain Brightspace access, and why both matter for grading and course evaluations.

How courses are assigned

Courses are assigned by the Department Chair using a Change of Instructor form. The form must indicate the primary instructor with a "P". The Chair completes the form and submits it to the Registrar; once the Registrar approves it, the faculty member is added into the system. Only the Registrar enrolls instructors into a course. CTRE does not enroll instructors.

Two things that depend on being the assigned, primary instructor:
  • Grading. You can only enter grades if you are labeled as the primary instructor ("P") for the course.
  • Course evaluations. Evaluations run based on the instructor(s) listed in the course. If you have not been assigned the course by your Chair and you do not have instructor access in Brightspace, your course will not be evaluated for you.

Brightspace access

Faculty will not have access to Brightspace unless they request access before the Chair enrolls them in a course. Brightspace courses are added to the system one to two months ahead of the upcoming semester.

Who you can and cannot enroll

As an instructor in your course, you may enroll your Department Chair (as Chair) and a course reviewer. You cannot enroll students, or other instructors teaching the course — those enrollments come from the Registrar.

Instructor vs. assisting instructor

  • Instructor: you must be enrolled by the Registrar. CTRE will not enroll instructors into a course.
  • Assisting instructor: a support role for the instructor who is teaching — useful for first-time instructors or for help with course creation. To request the assisting-instructor role, email elearning@csu.edu or submit a Zendesk ticket.

When students can see your course

By default, a course opens to students on the first day the course begins. Many instructors open it about a week earlier; if you are ready sooner, you can adjust the start date yourself.

To change when students can access the course:

  1. Open your course in Brightspace.
  2. Go to Course Admin.
  3. Select Course Offering Information.
  4. Scroll down to the Start Date and adjust it.
  5. Click Save.

Copying a course

To copy content on your own, you must be enrolled in the previous course as an instructor or an assisting instructor. If you are not, email elearning@csu.edu for assistance.

How to copy from an old Brightspace course

  1. Go to your new (destination) course. Open the course you want to copy content into.
  2. Open the Copy tool. On the navbar, click Course Admin > Import/Export/Copy Components.
  3. Select your source course. Choose Copy Components from another Org Unit and click Search for offering to find the old course, then click Add Selected. (If you are copying from a template your course belongs to, choose Copy Components from Parent Template instead.)
  4. Choose what to copy. Click Copy All Components (D2L recommends this to keep associations intact, then delete anything you don't need afterward), or click Select Components to pick specific items.
  5. Optional — adjust dates. Check Offset all dates of copied components to shift all dates by a set number of days and hours.
  6. Finish. Click Finish to run the copy.
  7. Review your results. From here you can copy another package, view the copied content, or review and manage course dates.
Good to know: the copy job runs in the background, so large courses won't time out — use the View History link to check progress. Any file from the source course with the same name will overwrite the matching file in your destination course, so rename files beforehand if you want to keep both.

Simple Syllabus Launching Fall 2026

Simple Syllabus is launching at CSU in Fall 2026. It is a centralized, template-driven platform that lets instructors quickly personalize and publish interactive class syllabi directly within Brightspace.

How to access: open your course, click My Materials, and choose My Syllabus.

What Simple Syllabus is

Instead of building a syllabus from scratch each term, faculty start from a campus template that automatically fills in standardized sections and required policies. You personalize the parts that are yours — outcomes, schedule, assignments, grading — and publish. Once published, the syllabus is stored in a central, searchable repository and is available to students in web, mobile, and print formats.

Benefits for faculty

Saves time

Templates auto-populate standard sections and required policies, so you are not re-entering the same information every semester. Copying a syllabus from one term to the next is quick.

Consistency & compliance

Required institutional policies and statements are built in, helping syllabi meet accessibility, accreditation, and institutional standards without you tracking every rule.

Easy for students

Students access current and past syllabi from one central location on any device, with a consistent, readable layout.

Works inside Brightspace

The tool lives in your course, and course details can populate automatically, so information stays accurate and up to date.

More detailed guidance and training will be shared as the Fall 2026 launch approaches. Questions? Email elearning@csu.edu.

Academic Calendar Logic

How CSU builds each academic year. Full schedule: csu.edu/coursebulletin/acadcalendar.

  • The academic year is two equal 16-week semesters (Fall & Spring) plus a 10-week Summer session.
  • Intersession is a 4-week semester housed under Spring; it starts the Wednesday after Fall grades are due.
  • The 12-week sessions in Fall and Spring start the 4th Monday of the term.
  • Spring Break falls between the 1st and 2nd 8-week parts of term.
  • Fall starts the third Monday of August (or the fourth Monday if Thanksgiving weekend would otherwise be the last day of classes).
  • Summer term begins the day after Memorial Day.
  • Final grades are due in CSU X-Press the Tuesday after final exam week.
  • Commencement is the Thursday before the term ends. There are no Summer or Fall ceremonies.
  • All terms end on a Friday.

Submitting Grades in CSU X-Press

Walkthrough for midterm and final grade submission. For training, check with your Chair and/or Dean first. For technical issues, email registrar@csu.edu.

Navigate to CSU X-Press

  1. Log in at ssb.csu.edu/PROD/twbkwbis.P_WWWLogin using your CSU ID (your "900#") and the PIN/password you set after your first login.
  2. From the welcome screen, click the Faculty Services link (or tab).
  1. Under Faculty Services, select Mid Term Grades or Final Grades. Grade entry opens based on the term schedule.

Enter grades in the worksheet

  1. Choose your course from the drop-down to open the grade worksheet, where your roster appears.
  2. For each student, use the grade-column drop-down to select the earned grade. If a student withdrew, a "W" appears — do not change it.
  3. Work down the roster. Scroll to the bottom and click Submit often so your session does not time out (the system times out after ~40 minutes).
  4. For more than one course, use Faculty Detail Schedule at the bottom to display your other courses.
  5. After entering all grades for every course, verify and confirm everything submitted correctly.

Grading notes

CodeMeaning
A, B, C, D, FStandard graded courses; calculated in the GPA.
PPass; only for non-punitive courses; does not calculate in GPA. Do not issue for courses that require normal grades.
WWithdrawal already recorded; do not change.
IIncomplete; can now be entered directly in the final grade worksheet in CSU X-Press (see below).
Incomplete ("I") grades — new process: "I" grades can now be submitted directly in the final grade worksheet in CSU X-Press. Note that submitting an "I" in X-Press does not notify Brightspace. To request an extension for a student to keep working in the Brightspace course, faculty submit a request via this form: Incomplete Student – Fill out form. An Incomplete Contract must still be completed and signed by student, faculty, and Chair, and the student must have (1) completed 50% of graded work, (2) be earning at least a D for completed work, and (3) have attended or participated within 3 weeks of the last day of classes. Contracts are due no later than the final-grade submission deadline.
Also note: WA and WD codes cannot be entered at final grading (past all withdrawal periods). Do not remove previously recorded grades — contact the Registrar (registrar@csu.edu or x2522) about any discrepancy. Grades roll to transcripts after the end of term, so students see updated grades/GPA the week after grades are due.

Faculty Portfolios

Faculty portfolios are for Unit A and Unit B faculty only. Portfolios live in Watermark Faculty Success. Log in through the Faculty Success & Course Evaluations login (the same link is used for Course Evaluations) or via Cougar Connect with your CSU email and password, then choose Faculty Success (Portfolio) for annual review, promotion, and tenure. For how-to support, contact CTRE.

Review requirements by faculty type

Unit A & Unit B faculty (not tenured)

Non-tenured Unit A and Unit B faculty need a Chair evaluation and Peer evaluation(s) for every review cycle.

Tenured faculty

Tenured faculty review follows a different process, as provided by the contract and the administration office.

Unit B lecturer classifications

Full-time Unit B

Started on the first day of the first semester (Fall) and taught more than 17 CUEs in an academic year.

Part-time Unit B

Started in the second semester and taught between 6 and 11 CUEs a semester, having done so for two semesters in a row.

Departmental Application Criteria (DAC) & annual review

Some documents below open inside Brightspace and require Brightspace access.

Reference the Contract Information, the Contract Overview for Faculty Training (requires Brightspace access), the Planning Sheet (requires Brightspace access; download to open the Excel sheet) to map criteria each year to meet retention, and the Faculty Portfolio Guide Book (requires Brightspace access). Annual review reminders include student evaluations for the most recent semester, peer evaluation(s), and the chair evaluation.

Adjunct Faculty

Adjunct faculty are those who teach fewer than 6 CUEs a semester.

  • Adjunct faculty are reviewed by their department chair.
  • They need a Chair evaluation each semester.
  • Adjunct faculty are not able to join the union.

Course Evaluations

Course Evaluations are administered through Watermark. Log in through the Faculty Success & Course Evaluations login (the same link is used for Faculty Portfolios) or via Cougar Connect, then choose Course Evaluations and Surveys for student feedback on courses. For how-to support, contact CTRE.

Timeline & rules

  • Evaluations run for 2 weeks before finals week (as listed on Banner).
  • Evaluations always stop on the last day of class, which is that Friday. After that Friday, students cannot submit course evaluations — there are no exceptions.
  • Evaluations run based on the instructor(s) listed in the course. If you are not assigned to the course and do not have instructor access in Brightspace, your course will not be evaluated for you (see Course Assignments & Access).
  • Encourage students to respond — results factor into annual reviews.
  • Students are emailed before release and daily until they finish.
  • Faculty are emailed ~1 month before the start date to confirm which courses are included.
  • Results are released to faculty 2 weeks after the course end date.

Library Services

The CSU Library offers a range of resources and services to support faculty. Start at the Library Faculty Resources page.

Tips for faculty developing syllabi

A few tips from the Reference Department for academic department faculty as they develop syllabi for an upcoming semester:

  • When requiring students to find articles in library databases, remind them they will need their CSU email login and password to access the databases from off-campus and to use the library computers on campus.
  • Confirm that assigned resources (books, journals, etc.) are either in the CSU library collection or available through a full-text database the Library currently subscribes to.
  • If items are not available at CSU, make your personal copies available to Access Services staff so they can scan the assigned readings and place them on reserve.
  • Include a reminder that students need a valid student ID to request materials from the CSU library or the I-Share catalog.
  • In your syllabus, distinguish between database publishers or providers (e.g., EBSCO, FirstSearch, ProQuest, Gale) and databases (e.g., Academic Search Complete, Education Research Complete, ERIC). Databases are sometimes available through more than one provider.
Reference Department: the Reference Department is happy to help faculty locate materials. The Reference Desk is on the second floor of the library, across from the elevator, and can be reached by phone at (773) 995-2235.

Follett Bookstore & Follett Discover

Follett is the official home for course materials at CSU: bkstr.com/chicagostatestore. Follett Discover is the online tool inside Brightspace that lets faculty discover and adopt course materials, and lets students access their required and recommended materials from within the LMS.

Work with your Department Chair to submit and process book requests and to confirm adoption deadlines. Faculty may also use other publishers (Cengage, Pearson, McGraw-Hill) as appropriate. Watch the Follett Discover demo videos at follett.com/discover/training.cfm.

Getting started — access Follett Discover

  1. Log in to Brightspace, your Learning Management System.
  2. Select a course from the My Courses widget on your Brightspace homepage.
  1. Inside the course, click the My Materials link in the navigation bar, then click My Books to launch Follett Discover.

Follett Discover opens on the My Courses screen, showing your personalized courses for the upcoming term.

Submitting adoptions

Type a Subject to start discovering materials, or use the global search in the upper-right to find materials and supplies by keyword, author, title, or 13-digit ISBN.

Select Term

Switch between past, current, and future terms. If adoptions are open, you can start adopting for any available future term.

Course header

Manage adoptions, discover materials, upload your own content, and leave a message for students within each course.

Manage by Section

Submit and manage adoptions by individual section instead of at the course level.

Share

Email a copy of your adopted materials.

Viewing & adopting a material

The course-material details page shows the description, table of contents, the lowest price available to your students, and availability options such as rental or digital. Scroll down to see neighboring institutions that adopted the material, related items from the publisher, and what other instructors adopted.

  1. Select the material usage (for example, Required).
  2. Click Adopt to submit.

My Library — reuse past adoptions

Use the library to quickly re-adopt titles you have used before. Reach it from the My Library link on the dashboard or the Copy button within a course.

  1. Click the Copy button at the bottom of the page.
  2. Select all the materials you wish to adopt.
  3. Select the department and term.
  4. Select all the courses you want to adopt the materials for.
  5. Click Adopt Materials to submit.
Tip: create shelves to organize your library by subject or topic.

Manage course adoptions

Manage a course by selecting the course banner or the View all Materials link from the My Courses page. Within the course management screen you can update the discipline and subject, view the status of adopted materials, remove adopted materials, adopt items from your library, create custom course packs, continue discovering additional materials, and add instructions for your students.
